furnace_mite.name: The Furnace Mite
furnace_mite.title: Kiln spirit of residual furnace heat

mortal_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_001.text: At the foot of Azure Cloud, Lin Yue stood in a queue of applicants whose sleeves were cleaner than her. She was twenty-four, a kiln worker's daughter with a cracked thumbnail and no sensed qi. Above the recruitment terrace, cultivators crossed the mist on narrow blades. Yue watched until her neck hurt. She had spent seven years wanting to follow them and three winters learning that wanting could not lift even a grain of ash.

mortal_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_002.text: My name is Lin Yue. I have brought my own bedding, forty-three copper coins and a recommendation from the west kiln. I can carry clay, read a firing ledger and repair a cracked stove. I cannot sense spiritual energy. I have tried the public breath exercises every evening that work left me awake. I am asking for instruction, not a title.

mortal_003.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_003.text: Shen Qing placed a glazed testing bowl on the table. 'Hands above the rim. Let your breath stay ordinary.' Yue obeyed. The bowl remained the color of old milk. Around her, four other bowls grew pale veins of light. Qing waited through another exhalation and then removed a polished stone from beneath Yue's bowl. 'Again. This one is the blank. A proper test includes something that should not answer.'

mortal_004.speaker: narrator
mortal_004.text: Neither bowl answered. Yue tried to loosen her shoulders without making a show of it. The man behind her sighed loudly enough for everyone to hear. On the table lay admission tablets for the outer disciples, each already threaded with green cord. Qing drew a different tablet from the drawer. Its cord was plain hemp. It recorded a name, a work assignment and permission to return for another examination.

mortal_005.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_005.text: 'The first test says nothing reliable about your eventual limit. It does say we should not give you a gathering manual today.' Qing turned the hemp tablet over. 'There is a paid place on the lower terrace. You will work in the mornings. Conditioning and reading classes meet afterward. You buy ordinary meals from your wages. The examination is in eight weeks. The work continues if you fail it.'

mortal_006.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_006.text: Yue looked from the hemp cord to the green ones. She had imagined her first day ending with a sword and a robe. Instead, the mountain offered her a broom, a bed and the possibility of being told no twice. 'How many people pass after entering this way?' Qing named a number smaller than Yue hoped. Yue counted her coins again, then signed her own name.

mortal_007.speaker: narrator
mortal_007.text: The lower terrace was reached by four hundred steps. Yue climbed them with her rolled blanket, pausing twice where the rail had broken. Her room held three pallets and a window facing the underside of the floating mountain. At night its stone belly shone with arrays too distant to read. She unpacked an ordinary practice sword, a borrowed primer and the jade pendant her mother had given her seven years earlier.

mortal_008.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_008.text: The jade felt warm against her palm. It always had. Yue wrapped it in cloth and put it under her bedding before opening the primer. The first page described the lower dantian as a place where a reservoir might be built. It did not say that everyone already possessed a lake of power waiting to be discovered. Beneath the printed diagram, someone had written: Learn the exit before the entrance.

mortal_009.speaker: narrator
mortal_009.text: Before dawn, a wooden clapper sounded outside. Yue carried two buckets to the communal cistern. She tried the long exhalation from the primer while climbing and nearly dropped a bucket when her vision narrowed. Water struck her sandal. She caught the handle against her knee, leaving a bruise that would trouble her all week. No hidden current rose to steady her. The remaining water still needed carrying.

mortal_010.speaker: elder_yun
mortal_010.text: Elder Yun found her breathing too quickly beside the cistern. She set the buckets down. 'You are doing three jobs badly: carrying, breathing and proving something to people who are asleep. Put the water away first. Eat before class. If the bruise changes your step, tell the supervisor.' Her eyes lingered on her name tablet. Whatever she recognized, she kept it to herself.

mortal_011.speaker: narrator
mortal_011.text: The work ledger assigned her to the ash room. Ordinary charcoal had to be sorted from spiritual furnace grit with a wet sieve. The latter could burn through a sack long after a firing ended. Yue wore thick gloves and worked slowly enough to see her mistakes. By noon, her back ached. Her wages for the morning would buy two bowls of rice, a vegetable portion and a little lamp oil.

mortal_012.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_012.text: 'Sit where you can keep both feet supported,' Qing said in the practice room. 'Today we observe. No held breath, no imagined river, no drawing anything into your belly.' The lesson seemed offensively simple. Yue had spent years picturing a brilliant wheel inside herself. Now she was asked to notice when her jaw tightened. She noticed it every time another student whispered that they could feel the room.

mortal_013.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_013.text: The warmth came after thirty breaths. Yue almost raised her hand. Then she moved her fingers away from her thigh and the warmth disappeared. She wrote that down. On the next attempt her pulse seemed to travel into her thumb, but the sensation kept the same rhythm as her heart. She wrote that down too. At the bottom of the page she left the space for sensed qi empty.

mortal_014.speaker: narrator
mortal_014.text: By the fourth evening, the other workers had given her notebook a name: the Book of Nothing. Yue laughed once because it was easier than showing how much the joke hurt. Afterward she filled another page with posture, food and sleep. Those seemed too humble to belong beside cultivation diagrams. Yet the page recorded something she had never known before: she stopped noticing her breath reliably after skipping lunch.

mortal_015.speaker: elder_yun
mortal_015.text: 'An empty column is useful,' Yun told her. 'It prevents tomorrow's hope from rewriting yesterday's result.' She drew a line beneath her meal notes. 'Your body is not the enemy guarding your cultivation. It is where the work must happen. If you make it weak, the first real trace will have nowhere safe to go.' Yue did not like being advised to eat when she had asked how to become stronger.

mortal_016.speaker: narrator
mortal_016.text: The first conditioning class began with standing. Yue's thighs shook before the incense mark reached its first notch. She widened her feet to hide the tremor, and Qing tapped the outside of her knee with a wooden pointer. Three corrections later, Yue understood that the apparent stillness of a cultivator was full of small arrangements. Her own arrangement collapsed whenever she thought about how she looked from the door.

mortal_017.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_017.text: Qing wrote four words on the board: Skin, Sinew, Bone, Marrow. 'Body Tempering is preparation for spiritual load. These names are assessments, not materials your body becomes. Skin means recoverable exposure. Sinew means aligned movement. Bone means supported load. Marrow means circulation sustained through work and rest. The last one is tested over a day, not during an impressive minute.'

mortal_018.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_018.text: Yue copied the words, leaving room beneath each. 'How long?' she asked. 'For you, we do not know yet,' Qing answered. 'Your first measure is eight weeks away. A stage can take a season, or longer when an injury intervenes.' Yue had saved for one season. She stared at the spaces under the words and began calculating how many morning shifts she could work without losing the afternoons.

mortal_019.speaker: narrator
mortal_019.text: On the seventh day, rain flooded the ash-room gutter. The supervisor offered an extra paid shift clearing it. The practice room would be open at the same hour. Yue's rice jar was nearly empty. Her left knee still hurt when she climbed. For the first time, the choice of how to cultivate arrived without a glowing sword or a dramatic enemy. It arrived as three possible uses of an afternoon.

mortal_first_choice.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_first_choice.text: Yue laid her work token beside the primer. She could earn food, practice a careful observation lesson, or ask someone to inspect the knee she had been hiding. Each answer would leave something else waiting. She crossed out the plan to do all three before nightfall. That plan had been written by someone who did not intend to sleep.

choices.text: Take the gutter shift and buy enough food for the week.
Attend observation practice and record uncertain sensations.
Ask for a knee assessment and a lighter practice load.

mortal_work_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_work_001.text: The gutter smelled of wet ash. Yue worked with a hooked scraper while a second laborer held the basket. When her knee stiffened, she changed tasks rather than insisting on another climb. They finished after the bell. Her extra coins paid for grain and a strip of dried fish. The supervisor marked the careful disposal of furnace grit beside her name. There was no mark for talent.

mortal_work_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_work_002.text: At supper, Yue tried to resent the absent practice hour. The fish made resentment difficult. She divided the grain into daily portions and left enough for one failed wage day. In her notebook she wrote: Worked instead of class. Then, after looking at the full jar, she added: Bought the chance to attend next week's classes without hunger.

mortal_study_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_study_001.text: The practice room was almost empty. Yue repeated the bowl exercise while Qing moved the calibrated stone without saying when. Yue called warmth three times. Only one call coincided with the stone. The other two came after she had tightened her shoulders. Qing did not award a partial success. Yue marked all three as uncertain and asked to repeat the comparison on a rested day.

mortal_study_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_study_002.text: She returned to a supper smaller than she wanted. Another worker sold her a portion of rice on credit, due after the next wage morning. Yue entered the debt beside the practice results. The lesson had bought clarity and cost a meal she had not yet paid for. She could see why wealthy applicants practiced more often. Knowing that did not change what her bowl had done.

mortal_recover_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_recover_001.text: The clinic assistant asked Yue to walk the length of the room before touching the knee. The bruise was ordinary, but the altered step was straining the opposite ankle. There was no spiritual wound to cleanse. Yue received a cold wrap, a reduced load and instructions to return if swelling grew. The assistant charged a small fixed fee and wrote down exactly what it covered.

mortal_recover_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_recover_002.text: For two days she carried half buckets. Other workers passed her on the steps. Shame moved more quickly than the pain, offering a dozen ways to prove she needed no concession. Yue used none of them. The swelling eased by the third morning. In her notebook, recovery took the space where she had wanted to put a new stage.

mortal_rejoin_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_001.text: The next lesson began with the accounts. Every student named their available hours, ordinary expenses and recovery time. Qing made no ranking of sacrifice. One student could afford four afternoons. Another could attend one. Yue was told to build a plan she could repeat for eight weeks. For the first time, the schedule on the board looked like something that might reach the examination instead of merely promising it.

mortal_rejoin_002.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_rejoin_002.text: 'The empty bowl exercise develops control of attention,' Qing said. 'A useful practice can remain ordinary. Do not add qi to its name because that makes the work sound important.' He passed around a practice talisman bearing three strokes. The last led toward a grounding mark. 'This is release. You will copy it with ordinary ink before anyone lets you draw the admission stroke.'

mortal_rejoin_003.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_003.text: Yue's first copy ended too close to the border. Her second ended inside it. On the third, she drew the line slowly enough that it touched the grounding mark without thickening. Nothing shone. The ink dried brown. Qing checked the direction with a finger and gave her a fresh page. Yue had expected praise for finally succeeding. She received the next repetition.

mortal_rejoin_004.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_rejoin_004.text: At night, the pendant grew warm beneath the bedding. Yue took it out and rested it beside the practice talisman. The talisman remained dull. She moved the jade over the bowl. Nothing answered there either. Seven years ago her mother had told her to carry the pendant to Azure Cloud when she could travel safely. She had never called it a cultivation manual. She put both objects away.

mortal_rejoin_005.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_005.text: Three weeks passed. Her standing practice lengthened by small measures. The ash room taught her hands to recognize grain sizes through the sieve. She could finish a morning shift without folding herself over the dining table afterward. These changes disappointed the part of her that had expected light. They helped the part that now had to earn lamp oil, copy a release stroke and wake again before dawn.

mortal_rejoin_006.speaker: elder_yun
mortal_rejoin_006.text: Yun watched her rub her thumb over a newly formed callus. 'Skin assessment next week,' she said. 'It is not how much abrasion you can endure today. We need to know whether you recover, whether you can notice damage early and whether yesterday's work leaves your hands steady enough for ordinary tasks.' Yue asked if that counted as cultivation. 'It counts as preparing a cultivator who might live through the next lesson.'

mortal_rejoin_007.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_007.text: For the assessment she moved a small basket of smooth stones, then a basket of coarse ones. Her gloves were inspected before and after. She reported a hot spot at the base of her thumb before it split. The examiner stopped that task and asked her to copy a release stroke. Her hand shook slightly. The result was recorded for comparison with the following morning.

mortal_rejoin_008.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_rejoin_008.text: Yue wanted the examiner to decide before sunset. She refused. At dawn, her hand had no new blister and the stroke was steadier. She marked Skin beside the first week of her conditioning record. The mark did not open a spiritual channel. It showed that the first load could be repeated. Yue read it five times before leaving, as if the ordinary ink might vanish when she stopped looking.

tempering_001.speaker: narrator
tempering_001.text: Sinew work began with a cord stretched between two posts. Yue moved a clay weight along it, keeping her wrist, elbow and shoulder in the same line. She had lifted heavier clay for years. The difficulty was releasing the weight without a jerk. Every time her pride chose a faster movement, the cord trembled and the lesson began again from the empty hand.

tempering_002.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_002.text: Qing demonstrated with no spiritual reinforcement. 'An external channel wash can help tissue recover. It cannot perform this movement for you. We will use none until your baseline is clear.' Beside his own practice mark he drew a second mark for Qi Gathering. 'You are preparing the road. Later you may admit a traveler. A wider road with nobody on it is still empty.'

tempering_003.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_003.text: Yue kept asking what qi felt like. Qing gave several answers and refused to make any one of them a rule. Coolness could come from sweat. Pressure could come from posture. Light behind closed eyes could come from squeezing them too hard. 'The sensation matters less than whether you can distinguish it from a blank and release it deliberately,' he said. Yue wished for an answer she could chase without checking.

tempering_004.speaker: narrator
tempering_004.text: In the sixth week, she tried to catch up with a student who had started younger. She doubled the cord weight after class. The first set felt manageable. The second left a bright ache down the inside of her forearm. By morning she could not hold the sieve without turning her wrist. The supervisor sent her to the clinic, and her record lost its next assessment date.

tempering_005.speaker: elder_yun
tempering_005.text: Yun found the extra weight beside her pallet. 'You have not lost the weeks you worked,' she said. 'You have lost the ability to use their result safely today. Those are different things.' She reduced her practice to ordinary walking and release strokes made with the uninjured hand. Yue asked whether she was punishing her. 'A tendon cannot understand punishment. It can understand load.'

tempering_006.speaker: narrator
tempering_006.text: For nine days, she worked at the ash ledger instead of the sieve. Her wages were smaller. She used the grain she had set aside and borrowed no medicine she could not repay. The younger student passed Sinew while Yue was still practicing without the cord. Yue congratulated him badly, with a voice that sounded too tight. Afterward she wrote the envy down without trying to turn it into a technique.

tempering_007.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_007.text: When the forearm stopped aching, the examiner still waited two more mornings before restoring the light weight. Yue had wanted to resume at the load she had lifted before the injury. She resumed below it. The slow movement felt humiliating until she noticed she could now feel the instant her shoulder began doing the wrist's job. That observation would not have appeared in a page titled Endured Everything.

tempering_008.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_008.text: 'Qi follows paths your body can sustain,' Qing told the class. 'It does not repair every error simply because it is spiritual. Reinforce a twisted knee and you may twist it harder. Send a stronger pulse through an unprepared bridge and you may break it. Before we teach admission, each of you will show me how to end an attempt that is going badly.'

tempering_009.speaker: narrator
tempering_009.text: The Sinew assessment used three weights and a request to stop midway through the second movement. Yue released cleanly. The examiner changed the angle of the cord for the third. She asked to reset her feet before lifting. She marked that request as part of the result. Two recovered days later, Sinew entered her record. There was still no light in the bowl.

tempering_010.speaker: narrator
tempering_010.text: Bone practice moved to a stone bench in the sheltered yard. There were no blows to endure and no cliff to leap from. Yue carried an increasing load across ten paces, set it down, then repeated after rest. She learned how much the bench supported while she adjusted her grip. Under fatigue, her body tried to take a shortcut by leaning. The examiner measured the lean rather than rewarding the load.

tempering_011.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_011.text: Her first letter home listed the wages before the stages. She explained the injury and the delay, although the paper would have held a simpler version where everything went well. She could not afford to send a gift. Instead she drew the release stroke below the account and described how it worked. She folded the letter around one ordinary sentence: I am still trying, and I can still work.

tempering_012.speaker: narrator
tempering_012.text: By the eighth week, the bowl test was due. Yue arrived with rested hands and a stomach full of millet. The calibrated stone was hidden beneath one of three bowls. She called the first one empty and the second uncertain. At the third, she felt a fine pressure that did not keep her pulse's rhythm. She identified it twice. On the final comparison, she identified the empty bowl as the stone.

tempering_013.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_013.text: 'There may be a faint mixed root,' Qing said. 'There is not yet a reliable result. We repeat in different room conditions next month.' Yue asked if she had failed. Qing answered yes, then turned the record to the page where Skin and Sinew remained. 'An unsuccessful sensing test does not erase the loads you can sustain. It changes which lesson comes next.'

tempering_014.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_014.text: Yue walked down to the wage office with the same hemp cord she had worn on her first day. The office offered another term. She could leave with enough money for the road home, or stay and earn another month's meals. She waited until the disappointment had stopped moving through her hands. Then she signed the term without pretending that the signature itself was a breakthrough.

tempering_015.speaker: narrator
tempering_015.text: The lower terrace did not celebrate her decision. A sack of grit had torn in the furnace corridor. Yue joined the cleanup after supper, marking contaminated tiles with chalk so nobody would carry the dust into the sleeping rooms. Behind the furnace door came a clicking noise. It stopped when she stopped sweeping, then began again beside a heap that should have been cold.

tempering_016.speaker: narrator
tempering_016.text: A furnace mite unfolded from the grit. Its shell was dark and layered like fired pottery. Between the plates shone a narrow orange heat. Yue had seen drawings in the disposal manual: a creature that fed on residual furnace qi and could spit hot particles when cornered. She held an ordinary broom. Her body had two tempering assessments. Neither made her skin safe against burning grit.

tempering_017.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_017.text: From the far end of the corridor, Qing raised one hand. 'Step toward me. Leave the sack. Keep its path to the hot grate open.' He was far enough away that Yue would have to pass the broken heap to reach him. Yue looked for something she could use without approaching the creature. Along the wall hung the soaked ash cloths and a long-handled clay scoop.

tempering_018.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_018.text: The mite clicked again. Yue had dreamed of a first battle where power answered the urgency of her need. Nothing answered now except what she remembered from work. The cloth could intercept loose grit. The scoop could shift a cold obstacle from the corridor. Her own task was to keep her face away from the heat and reach the marked safe line.

mortal_mite_choice.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_mite_choice.text: Yue could retreat behind a soaked cloth, clear the cold obstruction with the long scoop, or call the sleeping workers away from the corridor while Qing handled the animal. None required her to touch its shell. Her hand moved once toward the practice sword at her belt. Then she left it there. She knew how little an ordinary blade could change the temperature of flying grit.

choices.text: Shield the retreat with a soaked ash cloth.
Use the long scoop to clear its path to the grate.
Warn the workers and keep the corridor empty.

mite_cloth_001.speaker: narrator
mite_cloth_001.text: Yue lifted the soaked cloth between her face and the heap, leaving room at its side so the mite was not boxed in. A few hot grains struck the fibers and hissed. She backed toward Qing without trying to watch around the cloth. At the safe line, she lowered it onto the marked tile. One corner was scorched. The water on her glove had warmed, but her hand was unburned.

mite_cloth_002.speaker: shen_qing
mite_cloth_002.text: Qing guided the mite toward the open grate with a small grounded talisman. The creature followed the stronger heat and disappeared behind the protected mesh. 'You used the cloth within its rating,' he said. 'We replace it before another shift. A tool that saved you once may have less protection left.' Yue marked the damage on the disposal sheet and resisted describing the cloth as a shield technique.

mite_scoop_001.speaker: narrator
mite_scoop_001.text: The long scoop reached the cold shard blocking the grate approach. Yue moved it sideways a handspan at a time. The mite struck the handle once, leaving a blackened notch beyond her grip. She withdrew rather than taking a second strike. The gap was wide enough. Qing set a grounded lure beside it, and the creature crawled toward the heat it knew.

mite_scoop_002.speaker: lin_yue
mite_scoop_002.text: Yue wanted to keep the notched handle as evidence of her first victory. The supervisor told her to remove it from service. She wrote why on the repair tag: heat damage beyond the rated surface, strength uncertain. Her useful action had been moving an obstacle. The mite was alive, the corridor was clear, and the scoop needed repair. Those facts were enough for the report.

mite_warning_001.speaker: narrator
mite_warning_001.text: Yue called to the nearest sleeping room and asked its occupants to use the outer stair. She repeated the instruction until two people came out carrying their blankets in the correct direction. Behind her, Qing placed a lure by the grate. The mite followed it before the last room emptied. No one received a burn. Yue checked the rooms anyway, because the empty corridor did not tell her whether everyone had heard.

mite_warning_002.speaker: lin_yue
mite_warning_002.text: The supervisor thanked her for keeping people away and assigned her the next morning's return check. Yue had imagined praise would feel like a door opening. This praise came with another small task. She did it. At breakfast she listened to someone describe Qing's talisman as the entire incident, then added the warning route to the written record where the next worker could use it.

tempering_after_001.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_001.text: The incident report required no beast core and awarded no cultivation stage. The furnace grate received a new mesh guard. Yue's useful actions came from work she had once thought kept her away from cultivation. For the rest of the month she practiced with the same caution she used around hot grit: learn the limits, preserve a way out and do not trust excitement to measure distance.

tempering_after_002.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_002.text: Bone entered her record in the eleventh week. Marrow work began after it. She walked, worked, ate, practiced and slept while an examiner compared her morning and evening coordination. The task was continuity. A brilliant afternoon followed by an exhausted morning could not pass. Yue's first three-day attempt failed because she spent the last night's sleep copying a lesson she was afraid to forget.

tempering_after_003.speaker: elder_yun
tempering_after_003.text: Yun took away no book. She asked her to copy the same release stroke after breakfast. The line drifted before reaching the grounding mark. Yue could see the error. 'You chose an hour of study that made the next hour unusable,' she said. 'Write the net result, then plan again.' That evening she closed the primer before she had finished wanting to read it.

tempering_after_004.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_004.text: The next attempt included a shorter practice session and a full rest day before the comparison. Her ordinary strength had changed less than she hoped. Her steadiness had changed more. The examiner interrupted one movement, changed the next task and asked her to explain when she would stop. Yue answered without searching for a heroic reason to continue. Marrow was marked after the final recovered morning.

tempering_after_005.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_after_005.text: Across three recovered sessions in different rooms, Yue identified the calibrated stone and repeated the comparison after walking. Qing rearranged the bowls and included blanks in each session; she distinguished those too. Only after the third independent result did he record an ordinary mixed root with low admission efficiency. Three rooms in one sitting would not have satisfied the rule. Yue stared at the completed record. Seven years of wanting had not guaranteed it. Months of measured work had made a reliable test possible.

tempering_after_006.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_006.text: Permission to attempt admission came with a practice wick, a grounding mat and a limit small enough to disappoint her. The wick's light would measure one breath-unit at a time. Qing made Yue demonstrate the release stroke before placing the first stone in the room's array. The lower dantian was still only the site of a reservoir. Today they would learn whether a trace could enter and leave without injury.

tempering_after_007.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_after_007.text: The first trace felt cooler than her hand. Yue guided it into the external copper practice lead and lost it when a cup fell outside. Nothing remained after she stood. The second trace snagged near the old forearm injury before reaching the grounded lead. She released immediately and recorded the snag. This test opened no internal meridian pair. Qing ended the session. She had felt real qi, and the right final action was to let it go.

tempering_after_008.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_008.text: For six days she returned to low-load circulation without storage. The old injury set the pace. Admission that morning could mean no cord practice that afternoon. Yue learned to hate the calculation and then to do it anyway. The room's fuel ledger charged her sessions against a finite allowance. There would be no extra stone because she felt close. She used each attempt only after the previous day's tremor check.

tempering_after_009.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_after_009.text: 'Close the trace into the lower dantian,' Qing said. 'The external lead gives it a grounded exit; it does not supply a completed meridian.' Yue watched the imagined shape fail twice before she stopped imagining a lake. A smaller point remained when her breath changed. She stood, walked ten paces and returned. The wick glimmered for half an exhalation, then went dark. Clean release would precede any attempt to open an internal pair.

tempering_after_010.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_after_010.text: Half a breath-unit. Yue wrote the number with a hand that wanted to turn it into poetry. She waited through the next day before trying again. Her evening measurement was smaller, not larger. She had worked a full shift and skipped the short rest. She changed the schedule. The lesson did not care how important the previous evening had felt.

tempering_after_011.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_011.text: On the nineteenth day of admission practice, three breath-units remained after a quiet night. Yue did not receive a stage that morning. The test had to be repeated on separate days, with clean release and no next-day tremor. She lit the copper wick, watched three short glimmers and discharged what remained into the grounding mark. The room smelled of ordinary lamp oil. She went to work.

tempering_after_012.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_012.text: The second test passed after rain made the practice room colder. The third passed after a morning walk changed her breathing. Between them, Yue had one session where nothing stayed, and two sessions canceled for fatigue. The record kept all five results. When Qing drew the line under the final comparison, the failures remained above it. They showed what conditions the success actually depended on.

tempering_after_013.speaker: shen_qing
tempering_after_013.text: 'Qi Gathering, first stage: Trace,' Qing said. 'Three retained breath-units. Clean release. Stable recovered hand.' He handed Yue a green examination cord and left the hemp work tablet attached beneath it. 'You may learn to light a wick and reinforce a prepared movement later. You cannot bind a mountain, heal a tendon or draw sword aura. You have earned the first lesson in a larger kind of caution.'

tempering_after_014.speaker: lin_yue
tempering_after_014.text: Yue carried the two cords to her room and laid them beside the pendant. The jade had not changed. Her body had. Her notebook now held the bruise, the injury, the failed bowl tests, the meals, the debts and three successful morning measurements. She wrote home that she had entered the first stage. In the next sentence she wrote that she still worked in the ash room.

tempering_after_015.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_015.text: Two weeks later, the upper mountain began shedding blue dust. The practice arrays hummed beyond their normal range. Yue's wick lit too easily near the stair, then went out when Qing moved her to a protected room. The extra light belonged to the mountain's troubled field. It could not be added to Yue's measured reserve. The same correction that had once disappointed her now kept her from admitting a dangerous load.

tempering_after_016.speaker: elder_yun
tempering_after_016.text: Yun arrived at the lower terrace after dusk. She saw the pendant where Yue had laid it beside her notebook and finally said her mother's name. 'I asked her to bring that memory to the lake. She returned carrying it, and lost years she had meant to keep.' Yue stood. 'You told me to learn an exit before an entrance,' she said. 'Is that advice you followed?'

tempering_after_017.speaker: narrator
tempering_after_017.text: Yun accepted the question without answering it yet. She asked her to bring the pendant to the upper gate, by the protected stair and with Qing beside her. Yue packed her release notes along with the cloth around the jade. Ten thousand steps waited above the lower terrace. She knew how much her legs could carry and how little qi she could retain. For once, she climbed without confusing the two.

han_mei_shift.speaker: narrator
han_mei_shift.text: Han Mei ran the ash room with an old shoulder injury and a Bone-stage assessment she had never tried to turn into a higher title. 'The sieve needs a steady hand,' she told Yue. 'If yours stops being steady, come to the ledger bench. We still need the work done, and I would rather change a task than train another injury.' Yue looked at her hemp work tablet and recognized a life she had not included in her dreams.
